clue.text: It's a small world, as the ship's surgeon discovered

definitions.text: It's a small world, as the ship's surgeon discovered

parts.words: It's a small world, as the ship's surgeon discovered
parts.note: Gulliver, a ship's surgeon in Swift's satire, was shipwrecked on an island of tiny people: literally a small world

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks on a chance meeting, using the old saying about coincidences.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase 'It's a small world' is taken literally: Swift's hero Lemuel Gulliver was a ship's surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Gulliver's Travels names this island of six-inch-tall people, a realm in miniature.

clue.text: Liberality of interpretation in play

explanation.surface: Flexible readings of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom from narrow rules, giving scope or room to move, like slack in a rope.

clue.text: Young bride-snatcher takes the waters in a French department

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake
taken as written
the Var is a department in Provence

explanation.surface: A youth who eloped with a bride takes a spa cure somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Lochinvar, in Scott's poem Marmion, carries off his love from her wedding to another man.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's ballad hero rides in and seizes his sweetheart from her bridal feast.

clue.text: Anthem not exactly what's wanted as a formal presentation

indicators.note: not means without, so the second piece is removed

parts.note: an introit is a psalm or anthem sung at the opening of Mass
'that's it' means that's exactly what's wanted, so it gives IT

explanation.surface: An anthem that is not quite right for a ceremonial presentation.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction presents one person to another, a formal presentation of them.

clue.text: End of citation

parts.note: the word spoken aloud to close a quoted passage

explanation.definitionFit: Said after a quoted passage, it marks where the cited words finish.

clue.text: Player in the wind finds it a bit too — boisterous

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase too boisterous is taken, so the letters lie inside those words

explanation.surface: A wind player finds the band a little too rowdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player in the wind' suggests someone out in a gale; it means a woodwind player.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician on an oboe plays in the woodwind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Publican showing cunning in a drinking spree

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bender is a drinking binge
art means craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A pub landlord shows his guile during a drinking binge.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who serves drinks across a bar, loosely a pub keeper.

clue.text: Northern blockhouse

parts.note: a blockhouse is a military fort, but here it is a house built of blocks of snow in the Arctic

explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome dwelling of snow blocks found in the far north.

clue.text: He sets difficult subjects for doctorates

indicators.note: difficult implies the letters are hard to place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An examiner sets hard topics for doctoral students.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissertations submitted for a PhD argue a proposition, each one a thesis.

clue.text: Woodland deities brooded over the years

parts.note: a hen that brooded sat on its eggs
YRS is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Forest gods brooded over the passage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: These are half-goat spirits of Greek myth who roamed the forests with Dionysus.

clue.text: The historian has lost us, it goes without saying

indicators.note: the historian has lost something, so the named letters are taken out of his name

parts.note: Tacitus was the Roman historian of the early Empire
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a historian's account has left the listeners behind, which needs no saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being stated in words.

clue.text: As the correct procedure, start off the evening with a dance

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', that is 'as'
a drill is the correct routine or procedure for doing something

indicators.note: the start of the word evening supplies only its opening letter

explanation.surface: An etiquette guide says the proper way to begin an evening party is with a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille is a square dance for four couples, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: The study of friction — a cause of distress to boy and girl

indicators.note: distress suggests something knocked about, so the letters of to, boy and girl are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Friction between a boy and a girl causes them distress, presented as a scientific subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cause of' links the definition to the anagram of TO BOY GIRL, signalled by 'distress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribology is the science of interacting surfaces in relative motion, covering wear and lubrication.

clue.text: Point to a speck of dust and make a scene

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
a mote is a tiny particle, as of dust

explanation.surface: Someone points at a speck of dust and causes a fuss about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display exaggerated feeling, as in a theatrical outburst.

clue.text: Fall upon pass to a substitute

explanation.surface: A duty falls to someone who passes it on to a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty that falls upon someone devolves on them; delegating power to a deputy is also to devolve it.

clue.text: Nothing terminal resulting from his job?

definitions.text: Nothing terminal resulting from his job?

parts.words: Nothing terminal resulting from his job?
parts.note: this worker hopes nothing fatal comes of his job, since he works with big cats

explanation.surface: A worker hopes his line of work causes nothing fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's letters NOTHING TERMINAL cannot be an anagram (too many letters); it is a wry description of a dangerous trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who trains big cats risks a mauling every show.

clue.text: Quiet time on the Weald

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first in this across answer

parts.note: the Weald is a wooded region of south-east England, so it gives SE for south-east
a date is a fixed time

explanation.surface: A peaceful moment spent out in the Kent and Sussex countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a rural area spanning Kent, Sussex and Surrey in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, so peaceful in manner.

clue.text: Where the inmates are not tickled to death?

definitions.text: Where the inmates are not tickled to death?

parts.words: Where the inmates are not tickled to death?
parts.note: tickling is a poacher's way of catching fish by hand; here the fish are reared, not caught that way

explanation.surface: A grim institution where residents are not amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tickled to death' means delighted; trout tickling is the country trick of stroking a fish until it can be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm rears river fish in tanks for food or stocking.

clue.text: Jenny twice elected — bravo!

indicators.note: twice means that piece appears two times over

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey
a party elected to power is in

explanation.surface: A woman named Jenny wins two elections and is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo' looks like applause, but a bravo is a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is an old word for a hired thug or killer.

clue.text: Indian comprehending most of old language

indicators.note: comprehending means including, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada

indicators.note: most of the word old means its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An Indian who understands most of an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a tongue formed from a mixture of others that has become a community's mother tongue.

clue.text: Go round the Cape — start of exceptional thrill

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to exit is to go out
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

indicators.note: the start of the word exceptional is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sailing round the Cape is the beginning of a remarkable adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up strong feeling in someone is to arouse them.

clue.text: Love in Proust novel destroys

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
novel means new, so the letters of the author's name are given a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love features in a Proust novel and tears lives apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot something is to tear it out and wreck it, so to destroy it.

clue.text: Dig out her aunt's letters

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, giving AUNT

explanation.surface: Someone digs out an aunt's old correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something up from the ground, or bring hidden facts to light.

clue.text: One who has a bow for the coquettish queen

parts.note: arch means playfully knowing or coy
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A flirtatious queen takes a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows from a longbow; the clue's bow suggests a curtsey instead.

clue.text: Relax the terms of reference

explanation.surface: Someone eases off the rules of an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit a penalty is to relax it; a committee's remit is its brief or scope.

clue.text: Confused position of Irishmen reportedly on trial

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: Mick is a slang name for an Irishman
up before the court means on trial

explanation.surface: Irishmen said to be in court find themselves in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle or misunderstanding, a state of confusion.

clue.text: "Princess caught by lion", by Irish artist

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Leo is the lion of the zodiac
Pat is a stock nickname for an Irishman
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painting titled after a princess taken by a lion, by an Irish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen was a royal daughter of the Ptolemies before she ruled, a born princess.

clue.text: Paintings of small boys strike one

parts.note: to putt is to strike a golf ball gently on the green
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pictures of little lads are said to hit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherub-like infant figures in Renaissance art are called by this Italian plural.

clue.text: One of the six-footers Longfellow's Evangeline favoured

definitions.text: One of the six-footers Longfellow's Evangeline favoured

parts.words: One of the six-footers Longfellow's Evangeline favoured
parts.note: six-footers are verse lines of six metrical feet, not tall people; Longfellow wrote Evangeline in such lines

explanation.surface: A heroine in Longfellow's poem prefers tall men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall men, but a foot here is a unit of verse rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a line of verse with six metrical feet, the metre of Homer and of Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: Alexander's mistress was Siamese

explanation.surface: The conqueror's lover came from Siam.
explanation.definitionFit: Thais was the Athenian courtesan who accompanied Alexander the Great; people of Siam are now called by the plural of the national name.

clue.text: Note the wine account

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone looks at the bill for the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a spoken or written account of something.

clue.text: President who had to keep his end up

definitions.text: President who had to keep his end up

parts.words: President who had to keep his end up
parts.note: a person presiding at a meeting sits at one end of the table on a seat, so keeping his end up is literal

explanation.surface: A head of state who had to keep up appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep his end up' means do his share; here it is a seated end, as the presiding figure sits in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The person presiding over a committee or board takes the head seat, so is its president.
